parts.title: Lost in the mountains
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last summer, my brother and I decided to walk to a lake that we had seen on a map. The weather was beautiful, so we left our jackets in the car and took only a bottle of water and a few biscuits.

At first, the path was clear. But after two hours, we came to a fork where two paths went in different directions. The map was not very helpful, so we chose the left one. It was a mistake. After an hour, the path disappeared into the long grass.

We tried to go back, but everything looked the same. The sun began to go down, and the air turned cold. My brother wanted to run, but I remembered something that my father had taught me: stay calm, and follow a stream downhill, because it will lead to people.

We found a small stream and followed it. Two hours later, in the dark, we saw lights in the distance. It was a farm, and the farmer's wife gave us hot soup and a lift back to the car. Now I never go walking without a compass and a torch.

questions.explanation: They took a bottle of water and a few biscuits.

options: They met a very bad storm
questions.explanation: They chose the left path, which was a mistake.

questions.explanation: She never walks without a compass and a torch.

parts.title: How maps have changed
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
The first maps were very simple. [1] They were drawn on stone or on clay, and they often showed only a river or a village.

In the Middle Ages, maps became more beautiful. [2] Artists added sea monsters and strange animals to the empty places.

Then explorers began to sail round the world. [3] Each voyage brought new information, and mapmakers had to change their drawings again and again.

In the twentieth century, aeroplanes and satellites took photographs from above. [4] Maps could now be made much faster and with fewer mistakes.

Today, most of us use a phone instead of a paper map. [5] It knows exactly where we are, and it can tell us when to turn left or right.
sentences: Some people have never learned to read a paper map.
Many of them were more like pictures than useful guides.
People used them to remember where food and water were.
The result was much clearer and more exact than before.
It speaks to us through the screen or through headphones.
Cartographers could not agree about the size of the oceans.

gaps.explanation: People used simple maps to remember food and water; the next sentence says they were drawn on stone.
Many were more like pictures; the next sentence says artists added sea monsters.
Cartographers disagreed about the oceans; the next sentence says each voyage brought new information.
The result was clearer and more exact; the next sentence says maps could be made faster.
It speaks to us; the next sentence says it knows where we are and tells us when to turn.

parts.title: Using a compass
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: A compass is a simple tool that helps you find your way. It has a small needle that always points [1] the north. First, hold the compass flat in your hand and wait until the needle stops moving. Then turn your body slowly [2] you are facing the direction that you want. You should keep the compass away from metal, [3] it can change the way the needle moves. It is also a good idea to look at the map before you begin and to choose a landmark that you can see in the distance, such as a tower [4] a big tree. Walk towards it, and then take another reading. People often make the mistake of looking at the compass all the time [5] they walk, but this makes them trip. Practice in a park first, [6] you try it in the mountains.

gaps.explanation: The needle points to the north.
Turn slowly until you are facing the right direction.
Keep it away from metal because metal changes the needle.
A tower or a big tree gives two examples.
While they walk gives the time of the action.
Practise in a park before you try it in the mountains.

parts.title: Directions to a youth hostel
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: receptionist
turns.text: Thank you for booking with us. Here are the directions to our hostel. When you come out of the station, turn right and walk along the river for about five minutes. You will pass a large supermarket on your left. At the traffic lights, cross the bridge, and you will see a tall church. Our hostel is the yellow building opposite the church. The entrance is round the back, in a small garden. Reception is open from eight in the morning until midnight. If you arrive later, please phone this number, and I will come and open the door. Breakfast is served from seven thirty. If you get lost, do not worry. Many guests do, and the people in the corner shop know us well.

parts.title: An interview with a mountain guide
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Hart, you are a mountain guide. What is the most important rule of your job?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Never go without a plan. Before every trip, I check the map, the weather and the route, and I tell someone where we are going.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you use a phone or a map?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Both. But batteries die in the cold, so I always carry a paper map and a compass.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What was your scariest moment?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Once, fog covered the mountain, and I could not see two metres in front of me. We stopped for four hours and waited for it to clear.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Did your clients panic?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: One did, but I gave everyone a hot drink and told jokes. Staying calm is contagious.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you tell people who want to climb for the first time?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Start with an easy path, wear good boots and never be ashamed to turn back.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you still enjoy it after so many years?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: More than ever. Every mountain has a different story, and I learn something new every week.
